mainEntity.name: What is the best structure for a new business?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single best structure — it depends on your income, growth, asset exposure, and succession plans. A sole trader is cheapest but exposes personal assets; a company limits liability but adds administration; a trust offers flexibility but has distribution rules. The matched adviser assesses your situation and recommends the right structure — not a generic 'everyone should be a company' answer.

mainEntity.name: Can I change my business structure later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but a restructure can trigger CGT if not done under a rollover. Small-business CGT concessions and entity rollovers can preserve the position, but the conditions must be met precisely. The matched adviser plans the restructure to preserve concessions and avoid a taxable event.

mainEntity.name: Does a trust protect my assets?

acceptedAnswer.text: A discretionary trust can offer asset protection because beneficiaries do not own trust assets directly. But protection depends on the deed, your role, and how distributions are made. The matched adviser reviews your deed and structuring to ensure protection is genuine — not a label that fails under scrutiny.

mainEntity.name: How much does structuring advice cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A structure review and recommendation is typically $500–$2,000; a full entity establishment with registrations is usually $1,000–$3,000. The matched adviser gives you a clear quote after reviewing your situation — the matching is free.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will a matched structuring adviser contact me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your structuring needs.

mainEntity.name: Can a structuring adviser help with a partnership or joint venture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser structures partnership and joint-venture agreements, advises on profit-sharing and contribution terms, and ensures the entity type and deed support your commercial arrangement while protecting each party.

Yes. The matching service is free for individuals and businesses. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched firm, and the matched adviser gives you a clear quote before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: Can a structuring adviser help with succession planning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser structures your entities for exit-readiness — ensuring buy-sell agreements, share transfers and CGT concessions are set up correctly well before a sale or handover, so you maximise value and minimise tax on exit.

blocks.heading: Business Structures — what we can help with
blocks.text: SPECIALIST NETWORKBusiness Structures — what we can help withSole trader vs company vs trustSole trader is the simplest but exposes your personal assets and caps your tax planning. A company limits liability but introduces administration and a separate tax rate. A trust offers flexibility and asset protection but has distribution rules and compliance costs. The right structure depends on your income, growth plans, asset exposure, and succession intentions — not a template.Restructuring without triggering CGTMoving from one structure to another (sole trader to company, company to trust) can trigger a CGT event if done naively. Rollover relief exists under specific conditions — the small-business rollover, replacement-asset rollover, and entity restructuring — but the conditions must be met precisely. Our matched firms execute restructures cleanly, preserving CGT concessions where available.Asset protection and riskIf you hold significant assets (property, investments, IP), the right structure can protect them from business risk. Trading in a company while holding assets in a trust or separate entity is a common protective pattern. Our matched advisers assess your risk profile and structure for protection — not just tax.
